title: Tic‑Tac‑Toe solved, why still make a 3D version? — Quantum Grid's rules and juice
subtitle: In the already proven unsolvable Tic‑Tac‑Toe, how does adding 3D rotation and dynamic effects change the player experience? This article breaks down Quantum Grid's rules, AI, and presentation layer, exploring the separation of mechanics and aesthetics.
corePoints: Separation of rule layer and presentation layer
Juice changes the feel, never the rules

breakdown.title: Rule Framework
bullets: 3×3 board, X starts first, players alternate turns
Full board with no winner results in a draw, no failure penalty

breakdown.title: Turn Core Loop
bullets: Player places a piece → AI responds (minimax) → board rotates → render next frame
Rotation only changes perspective, not the logical positions of any cells
State machine: menu → gameplay → result, can restart or return to menu

breakdown.title: Presentation Layer Juice
bullets: Three.js 3D board with post‑turn rotation animation
Victory ribbons and Web Audio real‑time sound effects
